content: Unprecedented images may explain one of greatest mysteries of the sun Golden bands and swirling vortices have been spotted on the sun in the most detailed images ever captured of the turbulent surface of our home star. Astronomers observed the sun with the Inouye solar telescope in Hawaii, the world’s most powerful solar telescope, and saw new features smaller than 20km (12 miles) across in a magnetically active region close to a sun spot. The unprecedented pictures show processes on the surface that are likely to explain the decades-long mystery of why the corona, the sun’s outer atmosphere, is millions of degrees hotter than its surface. Read more: Icac resumes as factional ally of Angus Taylor due to appear next week The NSW Icac’s Operation Rosny hearings into corruption in the NSW Liberal party have resumed this morning, with Reformer Jean-Claude Perrottet, the younger brother of former premier, Dominic Perrottet, giving evidence again. Yesterday, he admitted he occasionally paid for memberships of people he was signing up to the Liberal party, which the inquiry has heard is against party rules. Branch stacking is not itself illegal, but the group is under investigation for allegedly soliciting or accepting illegal donations as part of branch-stacking efforts. Jean-Claude Perrottet has previously denied any wrongdoing, while Dominic Perrottet has not been named in any allegations by Icac. Icac has also announced next week’s witnesses. They include Jeremy Greenwood, who was originally scheduled to appear this week. He has been named in two allegations. The corruption watchdog is examining a second allegation that between 2020 and 2023, Liberal figures including Greenwood solicited or accepted donations from fugitive property developer Jean Nassif and his company, Toplace in exchange for the pursuit of outcomes sought by Nassif. Also expected to appear on Wednesday and Thursday next week is Catholic Schools NSW chief executive, Dallas McInerney. Icac is investigating the allegation that illegal donations were made by the schools governing body, arranged and approved by McInerney. Last week the inquiry heard a message sent by McInerney, who is a factional ally of federal opposition leader, Angus Taylor, to Reformer advising of a plan to “shake down Angus for 10K”. Taylor has not been named in Icac’s allegations and has denied he ever made payments to the Reformers. Man and pregnant woman found dead in outback Queensland home in apparent murder-suicide A sad update from our earlier post: A pregnant woman and a man have been found dead at a home in the outback Queensland town of Charleville, in an apparent murder-suicide after a protracted overnight standoff with police. Several streets in the remote town, 600km west of Toowoomba, were locked down by police on Wednesday evening after officers arrived at the property on King Street after reports of “a serious assault”. Read more here: Ed Husic looking forward to returning to full duties ‘shortly’ We have more from Ed Husic’s office following news he was injured in a car crash this week. Husic’s team wrote on Instagram: Mr Husic thanked the doctors, nurses and paramedics at Westmead Hospital for providing him with outstanding care and thanked his family and friends for their support, especially during his hospital stay. He said he looked forward to returning to full parliamentary duties shortly and assured constituents his electorate team would continue to support the people of Chifley in the meantime. Nearly 1,500 properties bought using first home buyers’ 5% deposit scheme converted into investments The government’s 5% deposit scheme for first home buyers has enabled the purchase of nearly 1,500 properties that were turned into investments, new data shows. The scheme is also helping hundreds of Australians earning more than $300,000 a year, after Labor stopped excluding high-income borrowers. First-time buyers can borrow 95% of a property’s value and have the government guarantee the loan, waiving costly lenders’ mortgage insurance, under the scheme. Housing Australia, which runs the program, provided the data in response to a Senate estimates question on notice in June. Read more here: A 60-year-old man has died after an alleged assault in Melbourne, where he was allegedly set upon by a group of youths. Victoria police said the man sustained critical injuries on 1 August after the group of young people allegedly attempted to steal items from a nearby store in the suburb of Sunshine. The victim allegedly came to the aid of a shop employee before he was attacked himself. The man was transported to hospital, but died yesterday, 5 August. Two boys, aged 12 and 15 and two girls, both 14, have been charged with affray, violent disorder and intentionally causing serious injury and injury. They have been remanded to appear before a children’s court. Earlier charges against a boy, 13, were dropped after investigations exonerated him. Detectives will consider upgrading the charges already laid after the man’s death. Labor MP Ed Husic taken to hospital with fractures and concussion after car accident Labor MP Ed Husic was hospitalised this week after his car was involved in an accident with a truck travelling on Sydney’s M7 motorway. The incident happened when the Chifley MP was travelling home from his electorate office, around 6.20pm on Tuesday, according to a spokesperson. Husic was treated by paramedics at the scene and taken to hospital for assessment and treatment. chineseContent: 前所未有的图像可以解释太阳最大的谜团之一在我们的母星湍流表面拍摄的最详细的图像中，人们在太阳上发现了金色的带子和旋转的漩涡。天文学家使用夏威夷的井上太阳望远镜（世界上最强大的太阳望远镜）观察太阳，并在靠近太阳黑子的磁活跃区域看到了直径小于 20 公里（12 英里）的新特征。这些前所未有的图片显示了表面的过程，可能解释了为什么日冕（太阳的外层大气）比其表面温度高数百万度这一长达数十年的谜团。阅读更多：廉政公署恢复作为安格斯·泰勒的派系盟友，将于下周出庭 新南威尔士州廉政公署针对新南威尔士州自由党腐败问题的“罗斯尼行动”听证会今天上午恢复，改革家、前总理多米尼克·佩罗泰的弟弟让-克洛德·佩罗泰再次提供证据。昨天，他承认他偶尔会为加入自由党的人支付党费，调查发现这违反了党的规定。分支机构堆积本身并不违法，但该组织因涉嫌在分支机构堆积活动中索取或接受非法捐款而受到调查。 Jean-Claude Perrottet 此前否认有任何不当行为，而 Dominic Perrottet 并未在廉署的任何指控中被点名。独立廉政公署还宣布了下周的证人名单。其中包括原定于本周露面的杰里米·格林伍德。他在两项指控中被点名。腐败监管机构正在审查第二项指控，即在 2020 年至 2023 年间，包括 Greenwood 在内的自由党人士向逃亡房地产开发商 Jean Nassif 及其公司 To 征求或接受捐款
